html:
Venezuela is a country on the Caribbean coast of South America, a separate republic since 1830. Under Spain it was a captaincy general tied to the Viceroyalty of New Granada, growing cocoa on slave plantations.

Caracas was the birthplace of Simón Bolívar, and Venezuela declared independence in 1811, one of the first Spanish colonies to do so. After a long and brutal war it became part of Gran Colombia, then left it in 1830.

The 1800s were an age of strongmen and civil wars. Then oil changed everything:

  • The dictator Juan Vicente Gómez ruled from 1908 to 1935 and opened the country to foreign oil companies.
  • Oil was struck around Lake Maracaibo, and by the end of the 1920s Venezuela was one of the world's largest oil exporters.
  • After the fall of the last dictator in 1958, the main parties shared power in a stable democracy. Venezuela helped found OPEC in 1960.

Oil money paid for cities and roads but left the country exposed when prices fell in the 1980s. Hugo Chávez, elected in 1998, used oil revenue for social programmes and took control of the courts, the army and the oil company. Under his successor Nicolás Maduro the economy collapsed, and the refugee crisis sent millions abroad. Venezuela still claims the Essequibo region held by Guyana.
sum: Venezuela is a country on the Caribbean coast of South America, a separate republic since 1830. Under Spain it was a captaincy general tied to the Viceroyalty of New Granada, growing cocoa on slave plantations.
